messages:
sara_support: Customer reports EU tenant showing eu-west in Console but traces + response headers show us-central. They saw higher latency and a cross-region charge. Request id: rq_3fb9c2. Need triage.

mike_oncall: can you paste the response headers or a raw trace capture?

sara_support: pasted from customer's curl capture:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Serving-Region: us-central-1
X-Redwood-Console-Region: eu-west-1
X-Request-ID: rq_3fb9c2
Latency: 420ms

Console screenshot attached by customer shows route badge = eu-west-1 for that model route.

alan_infra: interesting — serving header points to us-central which is authoritative for billing/latency. Console badge should reflect live routing state, but looks stale. @julia_console any known cache issues?

julia_console: we rolled a small change to the region-display cache last week to reduce UI calls to lookup service. It reads a prioritized POP map cached for 60s. If routing does immediate fallback due to capacity, badge can be stale until TTL expires. Not ideal.

mike_oncall: grep on gateway for rq_3fb9c2 shows route_decision payload: {"target":"us-central-1","reason":"capacity-eviction eu-west-1"}. Gateway forwarded to us-central pool.

alan_infra: so flow = console reads cache -> shows eu-west; gateway applies live policy -> falls back to us-central; response headers show actual serving region; billing uses headers. That explains discrepancy and cross-region billing.

sara_support: customer wants credit for cross-region fees and an explanation. Also they want to avoid surprises in future.

julia_console: short-term mitigation: surface a fallback indicator on the route row when any recent route_decision != preferred. I'll open a hotfix to show a subtle warning and include link to "served-from" header/info. Long-term: switch console to pull last-known route_decision from routing logs or subscribe to routing changes.

alan_infra: ops action items: 1) add metric for fallback-rate per route (alert if >0.5% over 5m). 2) index route_decision.reason in request logs for quick search. 3) provide one-off invoice credit for affected requests. I'll coordinate with billing.

mike_oncall: repro steps I used:
1) create project pinned to eu-west-1
2) run a load generator to saturate eu-west
auto-eviction triggers fallback to another POP
3) send request and inspect response headers
curl sample:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Look for X-Redwood-Serving-Region in response.

sara_support: updating customer now: "we found the cause (fallback due to capacity), billing is based on actual serving region, we will credit cross-region fees and ship a UI patch to show fallback events ASAP." :thumbsup:

deploy_bot: deploy started: ui-hotfix/region-badge-fallback-2026-03-18 -> prod

julia_console: created ticket RW-INC-6123 to track UI patch + docs update. Will follow up when prod deploy finishes.

sara_support: thanks everyone, will close after billing confirms credit and UI deploy verifies behavior.
